memory_candidates.content: In BimodalLogic (Typst reference-book work), a level-1 heading given custom real letter numbering via #set heading(numbering: fn, supplement: "X") positioned before the heading only wins over a document-wide #show heading.where(level:1): set heading(supplement: "Y") rule if the override is ALSO a show-set rule of the same shape, not a plain #set. A plain #set heading(supplement: ...) loses to an earlier document-wide show-set rule for the same field. Also: counter(heading).at(location) returns a multi-component array once any deeper-level heading has been seen in the document, and a single-placeholder numbering("1", ..state) pattern concatenates extra components with no separator when applied to that state -- this is the root cause of a #show ref rule rendering something like "Chapter 1534" for an unnumbered heading referenced late in a chapter-heavy document.

In this BimodalLogic repo, scripts/typst-status-counts.sh / typst-sync-check.sh Check 2 compares committed generated/status.typ against a live filesystem regeneration, not against git history -- so when a concurrent, unrelated task is actively committing to FormalSystem/ during another task's work, Check 2 drifts repeatedly and chasing it mid-phase is futile (the target keeps moving). The correct strategy is to only regenerate at natural checkpoints (a phase that already touches generated files, e.g. after Lean docstring edits) and at the final acceptance-gate phase, accepting that intermediate phases may show a stale Check 2 for reasons outside the task's own scope.
